In 6-dimensional [[geometry]], there are 64 [[uniform 6-polytope|uniform polytopes]] with B<sub>6</sub> symmetry. There are two regular forms, the [[6-orthoplex]], and [[6-cube]] with 12 and 64 vertices respectively. The 6-demicube is added with half the symmetry.

They can be visualized as symmetric [[orthographic projection]]s in [[Coxeter plane]]s of the B<sub>6</sub> Coxeter group, and other subgroups.
__TOC__

== Graphs ==
Symmetric [[orthographic projection]]s of these 64 polytopes can be made in the B<sub>6</sub>, B<sub>5</sub>, B<sub>4</sub>, B<sub>3</sub>, B<sub>2</sub>, A<sub>5</sub>, A<sub>3</sub>, [[Coxeter plane]]s. A<sub>k</sub> has ''[k+1]'' symmetry, and B<sub>k</sub> has ''[2k]'' symmetry.

These 64 polytopes are each shown in these 8 symmetry planes, with vertices and edges drawn, and vertices colored by the number of overlapping vertices in each projective position.
